In some estates [the custom] is that he must work [for] two days in each week, [doing] such work as he is directed to, throughout the year, and to work [for] three days each week during the harvest, and for three [days each week] from Candlemas to Easter. If he supplies horses for team-work, he need not work while his horses are out. He must pay ten pennies tax on Michaelmas day, and on the day of Martin’s Mass [he must give] twenty-three sesters of barley, and two hens; at Easter [he must give] a young sheep or two pennies. And from Martin’s Mass to Easter he must remain with the lord’s fold as often as it comes around to him. And from the time when one first ploughs to Martin’s Mass he must plough one acre each week, and collect the seed himself from the lord’s barn. In addition to that, [he must plough] three acres as compulsory service on demand and two [acres] pasturage-ploughing. If he needs more grass then he may earn it in such way as one allows him to. His plough-rent [is] to plough three acres and to sow [it with seed] from his own barn. And [he] pays his hearth-penny. As one of a pair [he must] feed a hunting dog. And each peasant pays six loaves to the lord’s swineherd when he drives his drove [of pigs] to woodland-pasture.

[4.a] On sumen lande is, þæt he sceal wyrcan to wicweorce II dagas swilc weorc, swilc him man tæcð, ofer geares fyrst ælcre wucan, 7 on hærfest III dagas to wicweorce 7 of Candelmæsse oð Eastran III; gif he aferað, ne ðearf he wyrcan ða hwile ðe his hors ute bið. [4.1] He sceal syllan on Michaeles mæssedæig X gafolp'. 7 on Martinus mæssedæg XXIII systra beres 7 II henfugelas, on Eastran an geong sceap oððe II p. [4.1a] 7 he sceal licgan of Martinus mæssan oð Eastran æt hlafordes falde swa oft swa him to begæð. [4.1b] 7 of ðam timan, ðe man ærest ereð, oð Martinus mæssan he sceal ælcre wucan erian I æcer 7 ræcan sylf þæt sæd on hlafordes berne; [4.1c] toeacan ðam III æceras to bene 7 II to gærsyrðe; gyf he maran gærses beðyrfe, ðonne earnige ðæs, swa him man ðafige; [4.2] his gauolyrðe III æceras erige 7 sawe of his aganum berne. [4.2a] 7 sylle his heorðpænig. [4.2b] 7 twegen 7 twegen fedan ænne headorhund. [4.2c] 7 ælc gebur sylle VI hlafas ðam inswa[ne], ðonne he his heorde to mæstene drife.
